title: Standing Instruction of the Credit Department: Service Charges on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts
content:
A service charge is assessed on an invoice of a Crop Input Purchasing Account still unpaid after its grace period, and the grace period is counted in whole calendar days from the due date of that invoice, the due date itself counting as day zero, an invoice cleared on the final day of grace attracting nothing.

## Clauses in force

**(a) The programme with no monthly rate.** A programme with no monthly percentage assesses no service charge at all, however long an invoice runs.

**(b) Reversal.** A service charge already assessed is reversed only where the invoice behind it is itself reversed by a credit memo or where the cooperative's own billing error put the invoice out; it is never reversed as a goodwill gesture at the desk, and a member who asks for it to be taken off on those grounds is passed to the credit department, whose decision that is.

## Clauses withdrawn

The words that stood here — *"The charge is the programme's monthly percentage on the unpaid balance of that invoice, assessed once per statement month for as long as it stands unpaid, and where the computed charge falls under the programme's floor the floor is assessed instead."* — are **no longer in force** on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts, having been superseded by the current basis on which the charge at the rate is worked out.

The words that stood here — *"It is assessed per invoice rather than on the account total, so a member with three overdue invoices carries three charges and three floors."* — are likewise no longer in force, having been superseded by the current basis on which the charge is worked out and booked.

## The grace period, both sides of it

The clock starts at the due date of the invoice, which is day zero, and runs in whole calendar days. The days of grace, the monthly rate and the floor are each the figure the member's programme carries in the credit department rate table. Taking a hypothetical programme whose grace is 15 days: an invoice cleared on the 15th day after its due date is cleared on the final day of grace and attracts nothing, while the same invoice still standing unpaid on the 16th day is past its grace period. The test is made against the cooperative's own record of the invoice — its due date, its number and the money it carries.

**Rate applied to the invoice amount.** The finance charge amount on an invoice is the invoice amount multiplied by the programme's monthly percentage, rounded to two decimal places, and where that is less than the programme's floor the floor is the amount. On a hypothetical invoice amount of 300.00 USD at a monthly percentage of 1.5 percent that is 4.50 USD; where the programme's floor is 5 USD, 5.00 USD is the amount.

superseded_clauses: The charge is the programme's monthly percentage on the unpaid balance of that invoice, assessed once per statement month for as long as it stands unpaid, and where the computed charge falls under the programme's floor the floor is assessed instead.
It is assessed per invoice rather than on the account total, so a member with three overdue invoices carries three charges and three floors.
